questions.question: Which list gives the six stages of the accounting cycle in the correct order?
options: Journals, source documents, ledger, trial balance, statements, final accounts
Source documents, journals, ledger, trial balance, final accounts, financial statements
Source documents, trial balance, journals, ledger, final accounts, statements
Ledger, journals, source documents, final accounts, trial balance, statements

questions.question: The process is called a cycle because:
options: Debits and credits rotate between accounts
The trial balance is prepared twice each month
The same fixed sequence repeats for every new accounting period
The owner checks the books in a rotating order

questions.question: The two questions the completed cycle finally answers for the owner of Khumalo Stores are:
options: Did the business make a profit, and what is its financial position
How many slips were printed, and who filed them
Which journal has the most lines, and which account is busiest
How much VAT was charged, and how many customers visited

subtopics.title: Stage One and Two — Source Documents and Journals

questions.question: Khumalo Stores sells goods for cash on 5 March. The source document produced and the journal it enters are:
options: An invoice, entered in the Creditors Journal
A receipt, entered in the Cash Payments Journal
A cash register slip, entered in the Petty Cash Journal
A cash register slip, entered in the Cash Receipts Journal

questions.question: Why are transactions sorted into journals before anything reaches the ledger?
options: Similar transactions are grouped so that only column totals are posted
The ledger may only be opened at year end
Journals work out the profit automatically
Source documents are too small to file

questions.question: What does the source-document stage deliver to the cycle?
options: A balance on every ledger account
Objective evidence of the date, amount and parties of each transaction
The net profit for the year
A list of posted totals in date order

questions.question: The assistant's wages are paid by electronic transfer. This entry belongs in the:
options: Cash Receipts Journal
Debtors Journal
Cash Payments Journal
Petty Cash Journal

subtopics.title: Stage Three and Four — Posting to the Ledger and the Trial Balance

questions.question: When the CRJ bank column total is posted at the end of March, the double entry is:
options: Debit Sales, credit Bank
Debit Bank, credit Capital
Debit Trading account, credit Bank
Debit Bank, credit Sales

questions.question: Journals are organised by date. The general ledger is organised:
options: By account, gathering every entry that affects one item
By the number on each source document
From the largest amount to the smallest
By the initials of the bookkeeper

questions.question: R700 paid for water and electricity was posted to the debit of Telephone, yet the trial balance still balances. This proves that the trial balance:
options: Will refuse to balance until the error is corrected
Checks arithmetic equality, not complete accuracy
Guarantees every amount sits in the correct account
Corrects wrong postings automatically at year end

subtopics.title: Stage Five and Six — Final Accounts and Financial Statements

questions.question: Gross profit is calculated in the Trading account and then transferred to:
options: The Capital account directly
The Bank account
The Profit and Loss account
The trial balance

questions.question: Net profit ends up in the Capital account because:
options: The bank insists on it
Profit belongs to the owner and increases owner's equity
Expenses are stored there until year end
The Trading account is closed to Bank

questions.question: The report that shows assets, equity and liabilities on the last day of the financial year is the:
options: Statement of Financial Position
Statement of Comprehensive Income
Trial balance
Trading account

questions.question: A cash sale's till slip amount eventually reaches the financial statements. The route it travels is:
options: Ledger, then CRJ, then final accounts, then trial balance, then statements
Trial balance, then ledger, then CRJ, then statements, then final accounts
CRJ, then trial balance, then ledger, then statements, then final accounts
CRJ, then ledger, then trial balance, then final accounts, then statements

subtopics.title: The Taxi Route Through the Books

questions.question: In the taxi-route picture, the ticket no passenger may board without is:
options: The trial balance
The source document
The owner's approval
The year's net profit

questions.question: Passengers queue at the rank in the journals because:
options: Eighty-five similar transactions travelling as one column total beats eighty-five separate trips to the ledger
Transactions must age for thirty days before posting
The ledger has limited space each day
Queuing is required by the bank

questions.question: The roll call at which left-hand totals must equal right-hand totals is the:
options: Final accounts
Source-document file
Financial statements
Trial balance

subtopics.title: One Slip Rides the Whole Route

questions.question: The R240 cash sale reaches the general ledger:
options: The moment the till slip prints
Only at year end, through the Trading account
As part of the CRJ column totals at month end
Never — cash sales bypass the ledger

questions.question: At posting, the R240 is delivered to TWO addresses, namely:
options: Sales and Capital
Bank and Sales — double entry at work
Bank and Drawings
Trading Stock and Sales

questions.question: By the time the owner reads the year's statements, Tuesday's R240 is:
options: Part of the profit story told by the Statement of Comprehensive Income
Still waiting in the journal queue
Written off as an expense
Shown as a liability to the customer

subtopics.title: The Three Clocks on the Wall

questions.question: The FAST clock, ticking daily, governs:
options: Drawing up the trial balance
Preparing the financial statements
The final accounts
Writing source documents and entering journal lines

questions.question: The MIDDLE clock, ticking monthly, governs:
options: Posting journal totals and proving the trial balance
Printing till slips
Transferring net profit to Capital
Issuing invoices to customers

questions.question: The final accounts and financial statements run on the SLOW yearly clock because:
options: They are the hardest documents to type
The big questions — is the business winning, and what is it worth — need a full year's story
Bookkeepers are only hired in December
Monthly profit calculations are not allowed
